title: pesto: target address mapping and netavark integration
body:
<!--- Please read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/containers/container-libs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before proceeding --->


- Add target address mapping to pesto CLI args so pasta forwards traffic directly to container IPs, removing the need for netavark DNAT rules.
- `portMappingsToPestoArgs` now generates `-t hostIP/hostPort:containerIP/containerPort`
- Add IPv6 `--map-guest-addr` for forwarding
- Call `PestoAddPorts`/`PestoDeletePorts` from netavark `Setup`/`Teardown`
- Skip netavark DNAT rules when pesto mode is active

Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28769
Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28770
Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28771

comments.body:
hey @Luap99 I was looking at why Total Success keeps failing here and I think the only thing actually broken is the _common fedora-current / lima_ job. Everything else in the run is green or skipped.

It isn't hanging though. I pulled the log and the cross builds keep progressing right up to the cancel, so it's just running past the timeout in `ci.yml.` `ci.sh` does `--cpus $(nproc)` and the runner is `cncf-ubuntu-2-8-x86`, so the VM only gets 2 cores.

#1019 already has the fix, it bumps the same job to `cncf-ubuntu-8-32-x86` and it passes there. might just need carrying over here.
